summary: Schedule model stages and microbatches while accounting for dependencies, bubbles and activation lifetimes.
outcomes: Draw a valid forward/backward microbatch schedule.
Estimate bubbles and activation memory for simple schedules.
sequence: Partition a sequential model into stages.
Trace one microbatch through forward and backward.
Introduce multiple microbatches and a fill/drain schedule.
Compare alternate schedules and stage imbalance.
Validate gradient equivalence and memory assumptions.

visual.question: Why is this stage idle and which activation must stay alive?
visual.interaction: Change microbatch count and stage costs; expose bubbles and lifetimes.

practice.task: Construct and compare two legal schedules for a small model.
practice.success: All dependencies and accumulation rules hold; throughput and memory tradeoffs are explained.
